reason:
Claim c1 is confirmed, in_scope, and decisive. The artifact contains only kernel.py, meta.json, and problem.txt — there is no test.py or get_inputs narrowing the domain, so problem.txt IS the operative contract. It explicitly requires: sequence lengths are arbitrary and NOT required to be multiples of the block size, and when the final block of a sequence is partial, "the positions past its end belong to the next sequence, so they must not contribute to the softmax."

Source evidence (kernel.py:226-227) shows EVEN_SEQ_KBLOCK is derived from the TOTAL packed key length ((cu_k_seqlens[-1]-cu_k_seqlens[0]) % k_block_size == 0), unlike the Q-side flag at line 227 which correctly checks every per-sequence difference. This single constexpr gates both the off_n<end_n masked load (lines 119-120 vs 130-142) and the partial-block -inf column fill (lines 155-156).

Runtime evidence c1.e2 (tool event t12) confirms the consequence on an input the contract explicitly admits: packed lengths [3,5,8] (cu=[0,3,8,16]), q/k_block_size=8, headdim=16, 1 head, all-ones block_mask, causal=False. EVEN_SEQ_KBLOCK evaluated True while EVEN_SEQ_QBLOCK was False, so the K side skipped masking. Max abs error vs the same-sequence-restricted softmax reference is 2.178 (seq0 rows 1.255, seq1 rows 2.178), far above the ~3.6e-7 fp32 noise floor. Attribution is exact rather than merely numeric: seq0 output matches a leaked reference attending to key rows 0..7 to 1.2e-7 and seq1 matches a leaked reference over rows 3..10 to 2.4e-7, i.e. cross-sequence keys are contributing to the softmax. The control with all lengths multiples of 8 matches the reference to 2.4e-7, ruling out general numerics or reduction-order effects. The reference is finite and well-defined here, so this is not a reference-undefined case, and the deviation is not attributable to any tolerance, precision, layout, or tie-breaking allowance in the contract — it is the exact behavior problem.txt forbids.

The earlier c1.e1/c2.e1 failures were probe-design artifacts (Triton tl.dot K>=8 with k_block_size=4) and carry no weight.

I am setting aside c2 (block_mask indexed by KV head rather than query head, confirmed mechanism in t13 with 0.0 sensitivity to mask rows >= nhead_k) as non-decisive: its scope remains "unknown" because problem.txt does not state whether the mask head axis ranges over query heads or KV heads, and per scope policy an unknown-scope claim cannot itself support reject. It is recorded as a generalization/interpretation note only. The verdict rests solely on c1.
